analysis:
The supplied change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation only. The visible hunks are the "Last updated" date bump, the KV re-slice floor funding text (head lines 982-989), and the cluster health-file paragraph (head lines 3532-3540). Further hunks near head lines 5234-5376 are not visible in the supplied units; the patch excerpt is truncated there.

I reviewed the two head_text units (838-1644) against the threat model. The Nemotron Super prefix-cache text (head lines 850-875) describes durable checkpoints encrypted under the provider cache root. They are scoped by the authenticated cache scope, and are off without a scope. Checkpoints are bound to a pinned-SHA-256 artifact identity and a PromptContractIdentity. This is consistent with T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, scope folding, TTL). Nothing there loosens the 30-minute TTL, the account scoping, or the KEK purge.

The GLM and MiMo sections describe fail-closed behavior: retained native owners, refused reloads, and a shipped-template hash check. They also describe a weight-hash verification chain. VerifiedWeightHashStore (lines 1046-1049) registers a stored hash without re-reading weights while file identity (device, inode, size, mtime, ctime) is unchanged, and the load verifies again before serving. That is a documented design with a re-verify at load. It is not a regression introduced by this PR, and it relates to T-012 and T-027, which are pre-existing.

The re-slice floor text (lines 985-989) is a capacity/availability description. It does not change any security control.

No code, endpoint, authorization, attestation, or encryption behavior changed in the visible text, and no finding qualifies. Remaining uncertainty: the truncated patch hunks at head lines 5234-5376 and the cluster health-file env key (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE) were not visible. Any code behind the documented health-file split (ClusterServiceAgent.partHealthPath) is outside the supplied evidence, so the claim that the supervisor's PID-bound liveness guard is preserved is unverified. I flag that for deeper review.
